newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-ARSENAL DENIED TOP SPOT BY VILLA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-ARSENAL DENIED TOP SPOT BY VILLA.

text.p: Aston Villa twice came from behind to draw 2-2 at Arsenal on Saturday -- a result which deprived the Londoners first place in the English championship.

Ian Wright put Arsenal ahead in the 13th minute with his 22nd goal of the season, latching on to a Dennis Bergkamp pass and thumping a first-time shot into Mark Bosnich's bottom left-hand corner from the edge of the area.
It was some consolation for Wright, who heard just hours before kick-off his appeal against a three-match ban imposed after he was sent off at Nottingham Forest last weekend had been unsuccessful.

The England striker, top-scorer in the premier league this season with 15 goals, almost added a second before the interval when he ran on to another through-ball from Bergkamp and rounded Bosnich only to see his shot cleared off the line by England under-21 defender Riccardo Scimeca.
Arsenal dominated the rest of the half, denying Villa a single strike on target.
"If we'd have come in three or four-nil down it wouldn't have been a wrong reflection on the first half," Villa manager Brian Little acknowledged afterwards.
But Villa, smarting from a 2-0 home defeat by Chelsea on Thursday, were a different side in the second half with Irish international Andy Townsend and Mark Draper controlling the midfield.
They levelled through Serbian Savo Milosovic, who had been blotted out of the match by Arsenal's three centre-backs throughout the first hour.

Townsend swung a free-kick in from the Villa right, Draper headed the ball back across goal and Milosevic drove a left-foot volley past John Lukic, standing in for injured England goalkeeper David Seaman.

Six minutes later Arsenal were back in front thanks to a brilliant individual strike from Paul Merson, one of several Arsenal players sporting standard-issue red and white gloves on a bright but chilly afternoon in North London.
Collecting a pass from Steve Morrow, he ghosted across the face of goal, jinked past Steve Staunton and Scimeca and drove a firm shot into Bosnich's bottom left-hand corner.
Within seconds of the restart, Villa were back on level terms, Yorke beating the offside trap and planting a right-foot strike under Lukic.
Arsenal pressed hard in the closing 15 minutes but failed to find the winner which would have put them level on points with Liverpool at the top of the table.

"We played a good first half and should have killed the game but we couldn't," Arsenal's French boss Arsene Wenger said. "In the second half we weren't physically able to keep it up after all our effort in the first half."
The result, a repeat of the first league clash between the two championship rivals in September, meant Arsenal dropped to third, two points behind Liverpool.

Arsenal - 24-John Lukic, 3-Nigel Winterburn, 4-Patrick Vieira, 5-Steve Bould, 6-Tony Adams, 8-Ian Wright, 9-Paul Merson, 10-Dennis Bergkamp, 14-Martin Keown, 15-Ray Parlour, 19-Remi Garde (18-Steve Morrow 67).

Aston Villa - 1-Mark Bosnich, 3-Steve Staunton, 6-Andy Townsend, 7-Ian Taylor, 8-Mark Draper (11-Tommy Johnson 87), 9-Savo Milosevic, 10-Dwight Yorke, 14-Alan Wright, 15-Fernando Nelson, 16-Ugo Ehiogu, 20-Riccardo Scimeca.
